newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos stevedores must raise productivity - Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: Santos stevedores must raise productivity - Cosipa.

text.p: Brazilian steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) said stevedores at Santos port must increase their productivity over the next six months under an agreement struck on Wednesday.
The Santos Stevedores' Union earlier voted at an assembly to accept Cosipa's proposal, which allows them to share loading and unloading at the company's terminal with private workers.
Although the Cosipa terminal has been operating on a shared-work regime since April, the new proposal aims to increase stevedores' efficiency.
"Their productivity was not matching the productivity of Cosipa's own workers," said a company spokesman.

Under the new plan, if stevedores match private workers' productivity within two months, Cosipa will continue to let them load one out of two vessels at the terminal. If not, the ratio slips to one vessel out of three.
If after four months stevedores still do not match the productivity of private Cosipa workers, the ratio falls again to one out of four, the spokesman explained.
Stevedores staged two strikes at Santos in April in protest at the firm's decision to use only its own workers at its private terminal.

Cosipa last week said talks with unions had failed and announced it would begin using its own workers on an exclusive basis from August 4, a move which shipping agents feared could cause a fresh strike.
